spans.quote: Start out with three or seven long in-and-out breaths, thinking bud- with the in-breath, and dho with the out.

instructions.note: the text allows three or seven; the script uses three

spans.quote: Keep the meditation syllable as long as the breath.
Be clearly aware of each in-and-out breath.
Observe the breath as it goes in and out, noticing whether it’s comfortable or uncomfortable, broad or narrow, obstructed or free-flowing, fast or slow, short or long, warm or cool.

attention.note: observing the breath as a whole: shown as the breathing torso

spans.quote: If the breath doesn’t feel comfortable, adjust it until it does.
For instance, if breathing in long and out long is uncomfortable, try breathing in short and out short.

instructions.note: a condition every meditator can check now, so it is narrated as an invitation

spans.quote: As soon as you find that your breathing feels comfortable, let this comfortable breath sensation spread to the different parts of the body.
To begin with, inhale the breath sensation at the base of the skull and let it flow all the way down the spine.

path.note: “all the way down the spine” → the lowest point of the spine (grammar kanda, shown as the base of the spine); one sweep per breath (sweep-one-breath)

spans.quote: let it spread down your right leg to the sole of your foot, to the ends of your toes, and out into the air.

path.note: right leg → foot_R; the text’s order (right first for men, left first for women) is kept as the order of the two sweeps; the gender claim is not narrated

spans.quote: Inhale the breath sensation at the base of the skull again and let it spread down your spine, down your left leg to the ends of your toes, and out into the air.
Then let the breath from the base of the skull spread down over both shoulders, past your elbows and wrists, to the tips of your fingers, and out into the air.

path.note: both arms; the picture follows one arm (fingertips_R) and the narration says both

spans.quote: Let the breath at the base of the throat spread down the central nerve at the front of the body, past the lungs and liver, all the way down to the bladder and colon.

path.note: “down to the bladder and colon” → the belly region

spans.quote: Inhale the breath right at the middle of the chest and let it go all the way down to your intestines.
Let all these breath sensations spread so that they connect and flow together

locus.note: all the sensations connected → the whole body

instructions.note: the promised result (“greatly improved sense of well-being”) is not quoted or narrated

spans.quote: Learn four ways of adjusting the breath:
in long and out long,
in long and out short,
in short and out long,
in short and out short.
Breathe whichever way is most comfortable for you.

attention.note: the breath as a whole: the breathing torso

instructions.note: the player keeps its own natural pace; the narration invites the meditator to explore. No holds: none of the four ways includes one

spans.quote: Or, better yet, learn to breathe comfortably all four ways, because your physical condition and your breath are always changing.

instructions.exclude_reason: a longer-term training aim (learn all four), not a step inside one sitting; kept for Ask

spans.quote: Become acquainted with the bases or focal points for the mind—the resting spots of the breath
the tip of the nose
the middle of the head
the palate
the base of the throat
the breastbone (the tip of the sternum)
the navel (or a point just above it)
center your awareness on whichever one seems most comfortable
And don’t try to force the breath or put yourself into a trance.
Breathe freely and naturally.
Let the mind be at ease with the breath—but not to the point where it slips away.
If you suffer from frequent headaches or nervous problems, don’t focus on any spot above the base of the throat.

warnings: no spot above the base of the throat
instructions.exclude_reason: applied structurally: the beginner form drops the head bases (beginner_override.skip_stages), and the start card names it

spans.quote: Spread your awareness—your sense of conscious feeling—throughout the entire body.
Unite the breath sensations throughout the body, letting them flow together comfortably, keeping your awareness as broad as possible.
The ‘guests’ here are the signs (nimitta) and vagrant breaths that will tend to pass within the range of the breath you are dealing with
Don’t be pleased by what appears.
Don’t get upset or try to deny what appears.
Keep your mind on an even keel.

instructions.exclude_reason: conditional on signs appearing (no-nimitta-scripting); preloaded for Ask with Ajaan Lee’s handling: don’t be pleased or upset, keep an even keel

spans.quote: If you can’t control them, don’t have anything to do with them.
Be circumspect.
Consider carefully whatever appears, to see whether it’s trustworthy or not.
